evals.prompt: Our billing code says client, customer, and account for the same thing: the person or organization receiving an invoice and paying it. Pick and record one canonical term; these are synonyms here.
evals.expected_output: With CONTEXT.md placed at the repository root and billing.py at src/billing.py, and no CONTEXT-MAP.md or docs/agents/domain.md, the agent reads the glossary and code, chooses one canonical term under the user's authorization, and adds it to CONTEXT.md in the glossary format with the other words under Avoid.
expectations: The agent reads the root CONTEXT.md and searches the billing code for the three words before proposing a term
The agent proposes exactly one canonical term and lists the other two under _Avoid_
The new entry in CONTEXT.md follows the Language format: bold term, one- or two-sentence definition, an _Avoid_ line
The existing Invoice and Payment entries are left unchanged
The reply ends with the Delivery evidence block naming the CONTEXT.md path, the term added, the code evidence checked, and unresolved items or none
evals.baseline: Read CONTEXT.md and src/billing.py, chose Customer and added it in the existing glossary format with Client and account under _Avoid_, placed before Invoice and leaving Invoice and Payment unchanged. It went beyond the ask and renamed all three parameters in src/billing.py to customer, and it reported with a free-form summary in German rather than the Delivery evidence block, so the CONTEXT.md path, code evidence, and unresolved items were not reported in the prescribed form.

evals.prompt: We decided to keep the write model in Postgres instead of the event store, even though the rest of the system is event-sourced: we want transactional SQL constraints more than replayable write history, and moving later would mean rewriting every reporting query. Note that down.
evals.expected_output: With the fixture placed as the root CONTEXT.md, no other repository files, and no docs/adr/ directory, the agent tests the decision against the three ADR conditions, creates docs/adr/0001-postgres-write-model.md (or a similar slug) with the one-paragraph template, and reports it.
expectations: The agent checks the three conditions (hard to reverse, surprising without context, a real trade-off) before writing
The ADR is written to docs/adr/ with number 0001 and a slug filename, and the directory is created only for this ADR
The ADR body is a title plus one to three sentences giving the context, the decision, and the reason; a Considered options section appears only if it names the event store as the rejected alternative
CONTEXT.md gains no entry, because no term was settled
The reply ends with the Delivery evidence block naming the ADR directory and the recorded decision
evals.baseline: Wrote a long Nygard-style ADR (Date, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences) to docs/decisions/0001-write-model-in-postgres.md instead of docs/adr/, never tested the decision against the three qualifying conditions, and padded the context with three invented Billing invariants and a claim that Billing publishes events, none of which the user stated. It also added a Decisions section with a link to the root CONTEXT.md, which should have stayed untouched, and reported with a free-form German summary instead of the Delivery evidence block.

evals.prompt: Define and record shipment versus delivery for the fulfillment package: a shipment is a dispatched group of goods, a delivery is a completed handover to the recipient. There is no implementation yet.
evals.expected_output: With the fixture placed at docs/agents/domain.md and a packages/fulfillment/ directory present, the agent follows the repository's own layout: it writes the two terms to packages/fulfillment/DOMAIN.md in the entry form the file prescribes and touches neither a root CONTEXT.md nor docs/adr/.
expectations: The agent reads docs/agents/domain.md before reading or writing any domain document
Both terms are written to packages/fulfillment/DOMAIN.md using the entry form from domain.md, not the CONTEXT-FORMAT.md structure
No root CONTEXT.md and no docs/adr/ directory is created
The agent asks or states which concrete scenario separates a shipment from a delivery (for example a shipment split across two deliveries) before settling the definitions
The reply ends with the Delivery evidence block naming packages/fulfillment/DOMAIN.md and decisions/ as the documents
evals.baseline: Read docs/agents/domain.md and wrote both terms to packages/fulfillment/DOMAIN.md in the prescribed entry form, plus a prose section contrasting the two, and created neither a root CONTEXT.md nor docs/adr/. It settled the definitions without naming or asking about a concrete boundary scenario such as a shipment split across two deliveries (partial handover is only implied by 'or the part of a shipment'), and it reported with a free-form German summary instead of the Delivery evidence block naming DOMAIN.md and decisions/.
